segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Erica.
segments.zh: 我的名字是埃里卡。

segments.en: Today we're bringing you another one of our sports lessons and this time we're going to go to a boxing match.

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we're going to be learning a language that you can use if you're talking about boxing, but not only boxing, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们将学习一种语言，如果你在谈论拳击，你可以使用它，但不仅仅是拳击，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: We can also use this language for describing a fight or somebody that's fighting.
segments.zh: 我们也可以使用这种语言来描述战斗或正在战斗的人。

segments.en: Okay, so not that we're asking our listeners to get into fights, but if ever you see a fight, at least now you'll have the language to talk about it.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以不是我们要求我们的听众打架，但如果你看到战斗，至少现在你就会有语言来谈论它。

segments.en: So let's listen to a dialogue for the first time.

segments.en: We have the legendary Rocky Balboa at EnglishPod fighting for the heavyweight championship.
segments.zh: 我们有传奇的 Rocky Balboa 在 EnglishPod 争夺重量级冠军。

segments.en: So let's see what happens.
segments.zh: 那么让我们看看会发生什么。

segments.en: Welcome back, boxing fans.
segments.zh: 欢迎回来，拳击迷。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields and here with me is the man with the iron jaw, Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我是瑞克·菲尔兹，身边这位有“铁下巴”之称的，是鲍勃·科普兰。

segments.en: Thank you, Rick.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，Rick。

segments.en: We're coming to you live from Las Vegas.
segments.zh: 现在从拉斯维加斯为您现场直播。

segments.en: We're in the beautiful MGM Grand Hotel and Casino where the World Heavyweight Championship is about to get underway.
segments.zh: 这里是米高梅大酒店及赌场，世界重量级拳王争霸赛即将开始。

segments.en: That's right, Bob.
segments.zh: 没错，鲍勃。

segments.en: We're about to witness the legendary Italian stallion himself, Rocky Balboa, square off against his lifetime rival, Apollo Creed.
segments.zh: 传奇“意大利种马”洛奇·巴尔博亚，即将迎战他的宿敌阿波罗·奎迪。

segments.en: This will be a gruesome match for sure.
segments.zh: 这一定是场激烈的恶战。

segments.en: Both fighters are in the ring and we are about to begin.
segments.zh: 两位拳手已经走上拳台，比赛马上开始。

segments.en: In the blue corner, weighing in at 220 pounds, the former heavyweight champion of the world, the master of disaster, the one and only Apollo Creed.
segments.zh: 蓝角出场的是体重二百二十磅的前世界重量级拳王，“灾难大师”阿波罗·奎迪！

segments.en: In the red corner, weighing 218 pounds and with a record of 47 wins and 37 knockouts, the undefeated, undisputed heavyweight champion of the world, the Italian stallion, Rocky Balboa.
segments.zh: 红角出场的是体重二百一十八磅、四十七胜且三十七次击倒对手的不败世界重量级拳王，“意大利种马”洛奇·巴尔博亚！

segments.en: There's the bell and this fight is underway.
segments.zh: 铃声响起，比赛开始！

segments.en: Apollo quickly attacks Rocky with quick, strong jabs.
segments.zh: 阿波罗率先发起进攻，连续打出又快又重的刺拳。

segments.en: He dodges successfully and counterattacks with a strong right hook.
segments.zh: 洛奇成功闪开，以一记强劲的右勾拳反击。

segments.en: Apollo is cut.
segments.zh: 阿波罗挂彩了！

segments.en: Rocky landed a strong blow to his right eyebrow and cut him.
segments.zh: 洛奇重拳击中他的右眉，打出了伤口。

segments.en: This is his chance.
segments.zh: 这是他的机会。

segments.en: Rocky quickly throws a left, right, another left.
segments.zh: 洛奇迅速打出左拳、右拳，再一记左拳！

segments.en: Apollo is getting pounded.
segments.zh: 阿波罗正遭到猛攻。

segments.en: Apollo recovers with a powerful haymaker and catches Rocky off guard.
segments.zh: 阿波罗回敬一记重拳，打得洛奇措手不及。

segments.en: He's down.
segments.zh: 他倒下了。

segments.en: The ref starts the count.
segments.zh: 裁判开始读秒。

segments.en: One, two, three, four, five.
segments.zh: 一、二、三、四、五。

segments.en: Wow sounds like a great fight.
segments.zh: 哇，听起来是场精彩的比赛。

segments.en: Amazing fight and I don't know who's going to win.
segments.zh: 打得太精彩了，我不知道谁会赢。

segments.en: Rocky apparently got knocked down.
segments.zh: 洛基显然被击倒了。

segments.en: What do you think will happen?
segments.zh: 你认为会发生什么？

segments.en: Well, if I know anything about Rocky Balboa, he will not stay knocked down for long.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果我对 Rocky Balboa 有所了解，他不会长时间被击倒。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Let's take a look at some of the language we saw in this dialogue in Language Takeaway.

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Okay.

segments.en: Yeah, or a gruesome film.
segments.zh: 是的，或者是一部令人毛骨悚然的电影。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So, gruesome.
segments.zh: 所以，令人毛骨悚然。

segments.zh: 现在，他们提到两名拳手都在拳台上。

segments.en: Both fighters are in the ring.
segments.zh: 两名拳手都在拳台上。

segments.zh: 拳台。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, the ring is the physical space where they fight.
segments.zh: 所以，拳台就是他们比赛的实际场地。

segments.en: But isn't it square?

segments.zh: 是的，它是方形的。

segments.zh: 它其实不是圆形的，但被叫做 boxing ring（拳击台）。

segments.en: I'm not really sure why.
segments.zh: 我真的不知道为什么。

segments.en: Well, maybe one of our listeners knows and can tell us about that because I am not an expert on boxing.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许我们的一位听众知道并可以告诉我们这一点，因为我不是拳击专家。

segments.en: But what I do know is our next word.
segments.zh: 但我所知道的是我们的下一个词。

segments.en: They were describing Rocky Balboa's career and they said he had 37 knockouts.
segments.zh: 他们在描述洛基·巴尔博亚的职业生涯，说他有 37 次击倒对手获胜。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A knockout.
segments.zh: 一次击倒获胜。

segments.en: A knockout.
segments.zh: 一次击倒获胜。

segments.en: In this sense, knockout is a noun.
segments.zh: 从这个意义上说，knockout 是个名词。

segments.en: A knockout is when the fighter hits the other fighter and he falls to the ground and he can't get up in 10 seconds because he's tired, he's dizzy, he's hurt.
segments.zh: 击倒是指拳手击中对手后，对方倒在地上，十秒内起不来——因为他太累、头晕，或者受伤了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, that's a knockout.
segments.zh: 所以，这就是击倒获胜。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, it's a technical boxing word.
segments.zh: 所以，这是个拳击专业术语。

segments.en: It's the action of falling to the ground and not getting up.
segments.zh: 这是摔倒在地不站起来的动作。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But there's also a verb, to knock out.
segments.zh: 但它也可以作动词，to knock out。

segments.en: Or to knock someone out.
segments.zh: 或击倒某人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, when you say, I knocked this guy out.
segments.zh: 所以，当你说 I knocked this guy out 的时候。

segments.en: It means I hit him so hard that he fell to the floor and maybe he was unconscious for a while.
segments.zh: 这意味着我猛烈地击中他，以至于他倒在地上，也许他昏迷了一会儿。

segments.en: So, he fell asleep basically.
segments.zh: 所以，他基本上睡着了。

segments.en: Almost.
segments.zh: 差一点。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, it's very similar.
segments.zh: 所以，非常相似。

segments.en: The noun form to the verb form.
segments.zh: 动词形式的名词形式。

segments.en: So, basically, if you knock someone out, you get a knockout.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，如果你把某人击倒，你就得到一次击倒获胜。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, to knock someone out, a knockout.
segments.zh: 所以，to knock someone out，就是击倒获胜。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now, for our next word, we saw as Apollo quickly began to jab Rocky Balboa.
segments.zh: 现在看下一个词，我们看到阿波罗很快就开始用刺拳攻击洛基·巴尔博亚。

segments.en: So, the noun, a jab.
segments.zh: 所以，名词，一个刺拳。

segments.en: So, a jab.
segments.zh: 所以，a jab 就是刺拳。

segments.en: Quick jabs.
segments.zh: 快速的刺拳。

segments.en: So, a jab is a kind of punch, right?
segments.zh: 所以，刺拳就是一种出拳，对吧？

segments.en: It's a fast, short, but not very strong punch.
segments.zh: 它是快速、短促但不太重的一拳。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, a technical boxing word, a jab.
segments.zh: 所以，一个技术拳击词，一个刺拳。

segments.en: A jab.
segments.zh: 刺拳。

segments.en: So, it can also be a verb, right?
segments.zh: 所以，它也可以是一个动词，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, to jab.
segments.zh: 所以，动词 to jab。

segments.en: To jab.
segments.zh: 出刺拳。

segments.zh: 现在，阿波罗正在投掷刺拳，洛基开始躲避。

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And that's our next word, to dodge.
segments.zh: 这是我们的下一个词，躲避。

segments.en: Dodge.
segments.zh: 躲避。

segments.en: D-O-D-G-E.
segments.zh: 拼写是 D-O-D-G-E。

segments.en: To dodge.
segments.zh: 躲避。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, if you dodge, you're trying to avoid getting hit.
segments.zh: 所以，如果你躲避，你就试图避免被击中。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, you move your body so that you're not hit.
segments.zh: 所以，你移动你的身体，这样你就不会被击中。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Now, we can also use it in different ways.
segments.zh: 现在，我们也可以以不同的方式使用它。

segments.en: Not only do you dodge when somebody's trying to punch you.
segments.zh: 当有人试图打你时，你不仅会躲避。

segments.en: You can also, for example, dodge a bullet.
segments.zh: 例如，您也可以躲避子弹。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, when you dodge a bullet, you avoid some bad situation or some bad event.
segments.zh: 所以，当你躲避子弹时，你会避免一些糟糕的情况或一些糟糕的事件。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.zh: 我们有很多 dodge 用在其他语境中的例子。

segments.en: Example one.

segments.zh: 看到那个人在交通中躲避了吗？

segments.en: He's going to get hit by a car if he's not careful.
segments.zh: 如果他不小心，他会被车撞到。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: Well, the storm turned south.
segments.zh: 好吧，风暴向南转。

segments.en: So, it looks like we managed to dodge a bullet.
segments.zh: 所以，看起来我们设法躲避了一颗子弹。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: Look, you're the one who is in charge of sales and the numbers are down.
segments.zh: 看，你是负责销售的那一位，而且数字下降了。

segments.en: It's your problem, so stop trying to dodge your responsibilities.
segments.zh: 这是你的问题，所以不要试图躲避你的责任。

segments.en: Oh, dodgeball.
segments.zh: 哦，躲避球。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Same principle.
segments.zh: 原理一样。

segments.zh: 是的，但那是完全另一堂课了。

segments.zh: 我认为我们需要在这里专注于拳击词汇。

segments.en: So, the announcers said that Apollo is getting pounded.
segments.zh: 所以，播音员说阿波罗正在受到重创。

segments.en: To get pounded.
segments.zh: 被痛打。

segments.en: To get pounded.
segments.zh: 被痛打。

segments.en: They're getting hit really hard.

segments.en: And a lot.
segments.zh: 而且是很多下。

segments.en: Mm-hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.zh: 所以，要被捣烂。

segments.en: Get pounded.
segments.zh: 被捣碎。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, Apollo received a powerful haymaker.

segments.en: So, Marco, what does it mean?
segments.zh: 那么，马可，这是什么意思？

segments.en: Basically, it's a very strong, very wild punch.
segments.zh: 基本上，它是一记非常有力、非常狂野的重拳。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, you don't have really good form.
segments.zh: 所以，你没有真正好的形式。

segments.en: Your body is kind of moving all over the place.
segments.zh: 你的身体到处移动。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, you don't have much balance.
segments.zh: 所以，你没有太多的平衡。

segments.en: So, you just throw your entire body and your fist at someone to hit them as hard as you can.
segments.zh: 所以，你只需将整个身体和拳头扔给某人，以尽可能用力击打他们。

segments.en: That's a haymaker.
segments.zh: 这就是大摆拳。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.zh: 给你们讲一个拳击专业术语。

segments.zh: 所以，比赛即将开始，体育播音员说洛基巴尔博亚将与他的终生竞争对手对决。

segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: Lisa and Daniel squared off against each other in the marketing meeting today.
segments.zh: 丽莎和丹尼尔在今天的营销会议上互相争斗。

segments.en: They were both pretty angry.
segments.zh: 他们俩都很生气。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, great examples, and I think we can use it now not only in boxing, but in other situations.
segments.zh: 所以，很好的例子，我认为我们现在不仅可以在拳击中使用它，而且可以在其他情况下使用它。

segments.en: Now, Bob said that Rocky landed a strong blow.
segments.zh: 现在，鲍勃说洛基打出了一记重拳。

segments.en: To land a strong blow.
segments.zh: 打出强力打击。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, land a strong blow.
segments.zh: 于是，强势打击。

segments.en: Now, let's break this down.
segments.zh: 现在，让我们分解一下。

segments.en: So, a blow.
segments.zh: 所以，一击。

segments.en: A blow is a punch or a hit.
segments.zh: blow 就是一拳，或一次打击。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And when you land a strong blow, what happens?
segments.zh: 当你打出一记重拳时，会怎么样？

segments.en: You basically successfully hit your opponent with a punch or hit.
segments.zh: 你基本上是用一拳或一击成功打中了对手。

segments.en: So, you hit them, so your fist meets their body.
segments.zh: 所以，你击中了他们，所以你的拳头与他们的身体相遇。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: So, your fist landed on their body.
segments.zh: 所以，你的拳头落在了他们的身体上。

segments.en: Mm-hmm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: So, I could also change this a little bit.
segments.zh: 所以，我也可以稍微改变一下。

segments.en: I could say, I landed a punch.
segments.zh: 我可以说，我打了一拳。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Or in boxing terms, he landed a strong left jab.
segments.zh: 或者用拳击的说法，他打出一记有力的左刺拳。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, to land a blow.
segments.zh: 于是，要打击。

segments.en: The announcer described it as Rock threw a left.
segments.zh: 播音员说洛奇打出一记左拳。

segments.en: To throw a left.
segments.zh: 向左投掷。

segments.en: So, he said he threw a left and a right.
segments.zh: 所以，他说他扔了一个左右。

segments.en: Now again, we'll take this one apart.
segments.zh: 再说一遍，我们将把这一款拆开。

segments.en: So, a left.
segments.zh: 所以，a left 就是左拳。

segments.en: What are we talking about?
segments.zh: 我们在说什么？

segments.en: Basically, a left punch, but we can omit punch.
segments.zh: 基本上就是左拳，但可以省略 punch 这个词。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, it's a punch with your left hand, but the verb throw, you throw a left punch.
segments.zh: 所以，这是用左手出拳，但动词用 throw，即 throw a left punch。

segments.en: So, basically, you punch somebody with your left.
segments.zh: 所以，基本上，你用你的左手打了一个人。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, it's just another way of saying to punch someone.
segments.zh: 所以，这只是打人的另一种说法。

segments.en: To punch someone.
segments.zh: 打人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, Bob started to throw some punches at the other guy.
segments.zh: 于是，鲍勃开始向另一个人拳打脚踢。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Look over there.
segments.zh: 看看那边。

segments.en: That guy's throwing punches.
segments.zh: 那家伙在扔拳头。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, to throw a left.
segments.zh: 所以，to throw a left（打左拳）。

segments.en: To throw a punch.
segments.zh: 打一拳。

segments.en: Now, again, you can use this in a lot of different ways with a lot of different types of punches.
segments.zh: 现在，您可以再次使用许多不同类型的拳头以许多不同的方式使用它。

segments.en: So, you could say to throw a jab.
segments.zh: 所以，你可以说 to throw a jab（打刺拳）。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or throw an uppercut.
segments.zh: 或者打上勾拳。

segments.en: Or throw a hook.
segments.zh: 或者打勾拳。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, now that we've seen all these phrases, why don't we listen to the dialogue for the very last time and we'll come back in a little bit.
segments.zh: 既然我们已经看过这些短语，我们不妨最后再听一遍对话，稍后就回来。

segments.en: Welcome back, boxing fans.
segments.zh: 欢迎回来，拳击迷。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields, and here with me is the man with the iron jaw, Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我的名字是 Rick Fields，和我在一起的是铁颚的男人 Bob Copeland。

segments.en: Thank you, Rick.
segments.zh: 谢谢你，Rick。

segments.en: We're coming to you live from Las Vegas.
segments.zh: 现在从拉斯维加斯为您现场直播。

segments.en: We're in the beautiful MGM Grand Hotel and Casino, where the World Heavyweight Championship is about to get underway.
segments.zh: 我们在美丽的米高梅大酒店和赌场，世界重量级锦标赛即将开始。

segments.en: That's right, Bob.
segments.zh: 没错，鲍勃。

segments.en: We're about to witness the legendary Italian Stallion himself, Rocky Balboa, square off against his lifetime rival, Apollo Creed.
segments.zh: 我们即将见证传说中的意大利种马洛基·巴尔博亚（Rocky Balboa）与他的终生竞争对手阿波罗·克里德（Apollo Creed）对决。

segments.en: This will be a gruesome match for sure.
segments.zh: 这一定是场激烈的恶战。

segments.en: Both fighters are in the ring, and we are about to begin.
segments.zh: 两名战士都在擂台上，我们即将开始。

segments.en: In the blue corner, weighing in at 220 pounds, the former heavyweight champion of the world, the master of disaster, the one and only Apollo Creed.
segments.zh: 蓝角出场的是体重二百二十磅的前世界重量级拳王，“灾难大师”，独一无二的阿波罗·奎迪。

segments.en: In the red corner, weighing 218 pounds, and with a record of 47 wins and 37 knockouts, the undefeated, undisputed heavyweight champion of the world, the Italian Stallion, Rocky Balboa.
segments.zh: 红角出场的是体重二百一十八磅、战绩为四十七胜且三十七次击倒对手的不败、无可争议的世界重量级拳王，“意大利种马”洛奇·巴尔博亚。

segments.en: There's the bell, and this fight is underway.
segments.zh: 铃声响了，比赛开始了。

segments.en: Apollo quickly attacks Rocky with quick, strong jabs.
segments.zh: 阿波罗率先发起进攻，连续打出又快又重的刺拳。

segments.en: Rocky dodges successfully and counterattacks with a strong right hook.
segments.zh: 洛基成功躲避并用强力右勾拳进行反击。

segments.en: Apollo is cut.
segments.zh: 阿波罗挂彩了！

segments.en: Rocky landed a strong blow to his right eyebrow and cut him.
segments.zh: 洛奇重拳击中他的右眉，打出了伤口。

segments.en: This is his chance.
segments.zh: 这是他的机会。

segments.en: Rocky quickly throws a left, right, another left.
segments.zh: 洛奇迅速打出左拳、右拳，再一记左拳！

segments.en: Apollo is getting pounded.
segments.zh: 阿波罗正遭到猛攻。

segments.en: Apollo recovers with a powerful haymaker and catches Rocky off guard.
segments.zh: 阿波罗回敬一记重拳，打得洛奇措手不及。

segments.en: He's down.
segments.zh: 他倒下了。

segments.en: The ref starts the count.
segments.zh: 裁判开始读秒。

segments.en: One, two, three, four, five.
segments.zh: 一、二、三、四、五。

segments.en: So as I mentioned, Marco, I'm not really that much of a fan or that knowledgeable about boxing.
segments.zh: 所以正如我提到的，Marco，我算不上拳击迷，也不太了解拳击。

segments.en: And actually, this is becoming a theme in these sports lessons, isn't it?
segments.zh: 实际上，这正在成为这些体育课程的主题，不是吗？

segments.en: Well, boxing is a very popular sport in North America.
segments.zh: 好吧，拳击是北美一项非常受欢迎的运动。

segments.en: I'm not really that big of a fan, but I have seen a couple of matches.
segments.zh: 我不是真正的粉丝，但我看过几场比赛。

segments.en: And it's very interesting because as we saw in our dialogue, most big fights take place in Las Vegas at some big hotel.
segments.zh: 这很有意思，因为正如对话里看到的，大多数大型拳赛都在拉斯维加斯的某个大酒店举行。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But you said it's super popular and everyone wants to watch these matches.
segments.zh: 但是你说它超级受欢迎，每个人都想看这些比赛。

segments.en: And obviously, everyone can't go to Las Vegas.
segments.zh: 显然，每个人都不能去拉斯维加斯。

segments.en: So what's the common way for most people to watch these boxing matches?
segments.zh: 那么大多数人观看这些拳击比赛的常见方式是什么？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So in the United States, there's something very popular called pay-per-view.
segments.zh: 所以在美国，有一种非常流行的东西，叫做按次付费。

segments.en: And I'm sure in your countries, you have something similar.
segments.zh: 我敢肯定，在你们的国家，你也有类似的东西。

segments.en: Basically, pay-per-view, you can buy the fight so you can have access to it and watch it on your TV.
segments.zh: 基本上，按次付费，您可以购买战斗，这样您就可以访问它并在电视上观看它。

segments.en: But you only pay one time to watch like maybe two hours, right?
segments.zh: 但你只付一次钱，就能看大概两个小时的比赛，对吧？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So let's say you're at your house, it's six o'clock and the fight begins at eight.
segments.zh: 所以假设你在你家，现在是六点钟，战斗从八点开始。

segments.en: So you can call your TV cable company or maybe use on the internet with a credit card and they activate it on your TV so you can watch the fight.
segments.zh: 因此，您可以致电您的电视有线电视公司，或者在互联网上使用信用卡，他们会在您的电视上激活它，这样您就可以观看战斗。

segments.en: And when it's over, well, you finished watching it.
segments.zh: 当它结束时，好吧，你看完了。

segments.en: Now, it's pretty expensive, isn't it?
segments.zh: 现在，它很贵，不是吗？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Pay-per-view can be very expensive depending on what event it is because sometimes it's boxing matches, concerts or special events.
segments.zh: 按次付费可能会非常昂贵，这取决于它是什么活动，因为有时它是拳击比赛、音乐会或特殊活动。

segments.en: So it can maybe cost, I don't know, 60, 80, maybe $100.
segments.zh: 所以它可能会花费，我不知道，60、80，也许是 100 美元。

segments.en: So it's very popular for one house to buy the pay-per-view and then many friends come over and everyone chips in with five or $10 and everyone watches it on one TV.
segments.zh: 所以很常见的是，一户人家买下按次付费，然后很多朋友过来，每人凑个五到十美元，大家一起在一台电视上观看。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the pay-per-view boxing party, a common way to watch the sport in America.
segments.zh: 因此，按次付费的拳击派对是在美国观看这项运动的常见方式。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.zh: 你们喜欢吗？

segments.zh: 你知道吗？

segments.zh: 你们自己可能是拳击手吗？

segments.zh: 或前拳击手。
